en: So that's our AVL tree, and with that we
eliminated this worst case of the binary
search tree by balancing out the tree. Now
with that, we got rid of that worst case
time complexity which we have on the binary
search tree. Instead, now we always have O)
and no longer O since we now will never have
an unbalanced tree like this.
Because of our auto-balancing that's built
into the tree. And that's why we might
consider using an AVL tree if we tend to
work with data that might end up in this
kind of tree structure. If you, on the other
hand, know that you're going to use your
tree for data that will rarely be structured
like this, building an AVL tree might be
overkill because, of course, as you can see,
It is more code and whilst it has a better
worst-case time complexity, if you're never
facing that worst case,
building this kind of tree and all this kind
of logic of course makes little sense.
